rows.question: Do I need to touch out on the bus?
rows.answer:
No – on a bus you only need to **touch in** when you board; there is no touch‑out required.  

(See TfL’s “Touching in and out” guidance – buses and trams require only a touch‑in 【source】)

rows.question: What happens if I forget to tap out at the end of my Tube journey?
rows.answer:
If you forget to tap out, TfL can’t work out the correct fare, so it treats the journey as incomplete and charges you the **maximum fare** – which does **not count towards any daily or weekly cap**. In extreme cases (e.g., you didn’t tap in or out at either end) you could also be issued a penalty fare or face prosecution.  

If the missed tap‑out was due to a system‑controlled gate opening (e.g., at a major event), TfL may automatically complete the journey and refund any over‑charge to your Oyster or contactless account.  

Source: TfL “Touching in and out – What happens if you don’t touch in and out” [link](https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/how-to-pay-and-where-to-buy-tickets-and-oyster/pay-as-you-go/touching-in-and-out).

rows.question: Can I pay for the Tube with Google Pay on my phone?
rows.answer: Yes – you can use Google Pay on your phone to touch in and out on the Tube, just like a contactless bank card. It works the same way as other mobile‑payment methods (Apple Pay, Samsung Pay, etc.)【source】(https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/how-to-pay-and-where-to-buy-tickets-and-oyster/pay-as-you-go/contactless-and-mobile-pay-as-you-go)

rows.question: My Tube was 20 minutes late. Can I get a refund?
rows.answer:
No – TfL does not provide a refund or compensation for a Tube journey that arrives late. The Tube fare you paid is for the service you used, and delays on the Underground are not covered by a refund scheme.  

If you need more detail or want to raise a complaint, you can check TfL’s official guidance on refunds and compensation here: https://tfl.gov.uk (search “delay refund” or “compensation”).

rows.question: How does the Hopper fare work?
rows.answer:
The Hopper fare gives you unlimited bus and tram journeys for **£1.75** when you travel *within one hour of your first touch‑in* using the same Oyster card or contactless device. It works automatically for adult pay‑as‑you‑go fares (and the same discounted rates for eligible passengers).  

- Touch in on the first bus/tram, then you can hop on any other bus or tram up to 60 minutes later without paying again.  
- If your card has a negative balance after the first journey, the Hopper fare won’t apply – you must top up within that hour to be eligible.  

Source: [Bus and tram fares – Hopper fare](https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/find-fares/bus-and-tram-fares) (section “Hopper fare”).

rows.question: Which lines run the Night Tube?
rows.answer:
The Night Tube runs on the **Central, Jubilee, Northern, Piccadilly, Victoria and Waterloo & City lines** on Friday and Saturday nights.  

Source: TfL Night Tube page – “Current services” section【https://tfl.gov.uk/modes/tube/night-tube】.

rows.question: Can people over 60 travel free in London?
rows.answer:
Yes – people aged 60 or over who live in a London borough can get a **60+ London Oyster photocard**, which gives them free travel on most TfL services (bus, Tube, tram, DLR, London Overground and the Elizabeth line, except the West Drayton – Reading section).  

- **Weekdays:** free at any time **except** the morning peak window 04:30‑09:00.  
- **Weekends & bank holidays:** free all day.  

The photocard also provides free travel on many National Rail services, subject to similar time restrictions.  

Source: TfL “60+ London Oyster photocard” – *Travel on TfL* section【https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/free-and-discounted-travel/60-plus-oyster-photocard】.
